title: SoMa: Identifying, Exploring, and Understanding the DRAM Communication Scheduling Space for DNN Accelerators
problem: As on-chip buffers on DNN accelerators grow large enough to hold most single-layer weights, single-layer dataflow optimization no longer meaningfully reduces DRAM bandwidth pressure. Multi-layer fusion and DRAM communication scheduling (timing of prefetches and stores across fused layers) remain an open, poorly-characterized optimization problem.
method: SoMa introduces a Tensor-centric Notation (TCN) to formally represent and enumerate DRAM communication scheduling schemes across fused layer groups. An end-to-end scheduling compiler framework explores this space jointly optimizing prefetch timing, data store scheduling, and layer fusion decisions for diverse accelerators and workloads. SoMa has been deployed as a compiler for a commercial accelerator product.

title: InterConFuzz: A Fuzzing-based Comprehensive NoC Verification Framework
problem: Security verification of Network-on-Chip (NoC) systems is challenging due to intricate high-concurrency structures; traditional verification methods fail to achieve comprehensive coverage, leading to prolonged verification and overlooked security vulnerabilities.
method: InterConFuzz is a hybrid hardware fuzzing technique using symbolic execution for extensive coverage of NoC state space. Built on Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) for standard verification flow integration. Applies fuzzing to systematically explore NoC behaviors and identify security flaws in high-concurrency scenarios.

title: 5.9 A 21-to-31 GHz DPD-Less Quadrature RFDAC with Invariant Impedance and Scalable LO Leakage
problem: RF digital-to-analog converters (RFDACs) for mm-wave wireless transmitters (high-order QAM, wideband modulation) suffer nonlinearity increasing with frequency due to: (1) varied output impedance across unit array vs. baseband code, (2) distributed parasitics, (3) LO leakage. Existing solutions—DPD (complex, frequency-dependent), open-loop linearization (PVT-variant), self-calibration (loop-response-limited)—are inadequate; extra bits added for intrinsic nonlinearity compensation waste power in high-GS/s baseband.
method: DPD-less broadband mm-wave RFDAC (21–31GHz) with two key innovations: (1) invariant output impedance design ensuring unit-cell impedance independence from baseband code, eliminating impedance-induced nonlinearity; (2) scalable LO-leakage suppression technique adaptively reducing LO feedthrough across PVT conditions without feedback loops. Architecture achieves inherent linearity suitable for high-order QAM without requiring complex DPD, open-loop adaptation, or calibration loops.

title: Syno: Structured Synthesis for Neural Operators
problem: Neural architecture search (NAS) and tensor compilers both optimize over existing manually designed operators and cannot discover fundamentally new operator designs with better accuracy-performance tradeoffs. There is no systematic method to automatically synthesize novel neural operators that satisfy structural constraints required for trainability and hardware efficiency.
method: Syno defines a set of fine-grained primitives operating on tensor dimensions that enforce properties needed for stable model training (e.g., dimension matching, associativity). Expression canonicalization techniques prune redundant candidates during search. A guided synthesis flow constrains valid operators to specified input/output dimension sizes, and stochastic tree search (Monte Carlo-style) efficiently explores the large design space. The resulting operators are compiled and evaluated on real hardware.

title: Ares: High Performance Near-Storage Accelerator for FHE-based Private Set Intersection
problem: General-purpose FHE accelerators do not adequately address the unique requirements of Private Set Intersection applications, leading to suboptimal data handling, underutilization of hardware bandwidth, and inefficient deployment for PSI acceleration.
method: Ares is an FPGA accelerator co-designed with software, proposing Lazy Relinearization to optimize redundant PSI calculations, analyzing/decoupling PSI compute patterns into hardware kernels, and fully utilizing bandwidth and compute resources through specialized architecture design.

title: Coupling Static and Dynamic MPI Correctness Tools to Optimize Accuracy and Overhead
problem: Static MPI correctness tools produce false positives (lack runtime context); dynamic tools produce false negatives (limited coverage) and have high overhead. Combining them could improve accuracy while reducing overhead.
method: Coupled workflow forwarding static tool reports to dynamic tools; generic exchange format enabling interoperability; integration of CoVer (static), SPMD IR (static), and MUST (dynamic) for detecting MPI local data races; selective instrumentation of dynamic tool based on static hints

title: FIRST: Federated Inference Resource Scheduling Toolkit for Scientific AI Model Access
problem: Lack of scalable, on-premises AI inference infrastructure for scientific workloads with privacy constraints
method: Federated inference framework using Globus Auth/Compute, multiple inference backends (vLLM), auto-scaling with hot-node management

title: 20.10 A 200GHz 200-Pixel 2D Near-Field Imager for Biomedical Applications
problem: Near-field mmWave/THz imaging systems face challenges: (1) single-source/single-detector-per-pixel limits resolution scalability, (2) lack of proper isolated resonator selection methods, (3) poor resonator Q at high frequencies near lossy biological samples, limiting sensitivity.
method: A 200GHz 200-pixel 2D near-field imager uses four key techniques: (1) Q-boosted Active Split-Ring Resonators (ASRR) enable dense pixel integration with individual selection via minimal capacitive loading, (2) selective pixel activation using shared source/detector (not per-pixel), (3) phase detection replaces power/frequency detection to avoid high free-running VCO phase noise, (4) correlated-doubling sampling (CDS) suppresses low-frequency noise.

title: Evaluating Ruche Networks: Physically Scalable, Cost-Effective, Bandwidth-Flexible NoCs
problem: The standard 2-D mesh NoC topology suffers poor latency and throughput scaling for data-intensive manycore workloads, while prior solutions (concentrated routers, widened channels) rely on outdated assumptions that break under modern streaming-bandwidth requirements and impose significant additional cost. A rigorous, RTL-level evaluation of Ruche Networks as a superior alternative has not been performed.
method: Ruche Networks augment the 2-D mesh topology with uniform long-range bypass links (Ruche channels) that allow non-neighboring routers to communicate in fewer hops, preserving the physical scalability and regular structure of the mesh. The authors implement Ruche Networks at RTL level and compare against 2-D mesh and torus topologies under identical conditions, evaluating network throughput, latency, power consumption, area efficiency, and cycle time across manycore workloads with streaming bandwidth demands.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper MetoHash: A Memory-Efficient and Traffic-Optimized Hashing Index on Hybrid PMem-DRAM Memories
problem: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility assessment of hybrid persistent memory-DRAM hashing index
method: Artifact evaluation and testing following SC25 Reproducibility Initiative standards

title: PEAK: Cost-Adaptive Profiling in a Heartbeat
problem: Static instrumentation profiling imposes fixed overhead that cannot adapt to dynamic workload characteristics
method: Dynamic Binary Instrumentation (DBI) profiler with two modes: static (absolute overhead cap) and dynamic heartbeat (maintains user-defined relative overhead ratio)

title: SAPO: Improving the Scalability and Accuracy of Quantum Linear Solver for Portfolio Optimization
problem: Quantum linear solvers for portfolio optimization suffer from poor scalability or insufficient accuracy; existing quantum HHL-based methods cannot efficiently handle large-scale financial problems with acceptable precision.
method: SAPO extends the HHL algorithm by integrating mean-variance financial theory into the quantum circuit design via equivalent transformations to improve scalability, and applies a min-max eigenvalue model calibrated on historical market data to refine quantum circuit parameters for high accuracy.

title: ILAN: The Interference- and Locality-Aware NUMA Scheduler
problem: OpenMP default scheduler is topology-agnostic; poor data locality and task interference on NUMA systems
method: ILAN scheduler: moldability for interference mitigation + hierarchical scheduling for locality

title: ArtMem: Adaptive Migration in Reinforcement Learning-Enabled Tiered Memory
problem: Tiered memory systems struggle with three key inefficiencies: existing migration policies perform inconsistently across workloads, fail to adapt when the fast-tier access rate is low, and miss opportunities to tune migration scope dynamically based on workload patterns, causing unnecessary page migrations.
method: ArtMem is a reinforcement learning (RL)-driven tiered memory management framework that dynamically adapts migration policy to evolving workload behavior. The RL agent observes fast-tier access rates and workload access patterns at runtime to decide page placement, migration scope (which pages to migrate and how many), and when to suppress migration entirely when the fast tier is underutilized. This closed-loop control replaces static thresholds with learned policies.

title: Physical System Study on Balancing Interactive and Batch Job Performance through Oversubscribing Scheduling
problem: Interactive and batch jobs have conflicting resource requirements in shared HPC systems
method: Physical system study with real workloads; oversubscribing on actual hardware; memory usage analysis

title: 4th Gen AMD CDNA™ Generative AI Architecture Powering AMD Instinct M350 Series GPUs and Platforms
problem: Generative AI and LLM inference require GPU architectures optimized for transformer workloads with efficient memory bandwidth, tensor operations, and mixed-precision compute.
method: 4th Gen CDNA architecture enhances the previous generation with improved compute density, memory hierarchy, tensor cores, and specialized instructions for transformer operations and mixed-precision formats.
